data.text/markdown:
Chat Mode and Agent Mode in Numerical Calculation

A pre-run, read-only breakdown of the four quantities that a frontier model reported with material error in chat mode, recomputed here by program execution. The notebook executes automatically on load. For an editable version, open the MoLab notebook linked from the host page and edit the values there. Concentrations are in mol/L, times in min, flows in m^3/s, and costs in dollars/yr.

Step 1: The four recorded failures

Two modes of obtaining a number from a language model are compared. In chat mode, the answer is generated as text, token by token, and no program is executed at any point. In agent mode, the model writes a program, the program is executed, and the answer is read from the execution. On 24 October 2026, 26 undergraduate chemical-engineering problems were given to a frontier model (Muse Spark 1.3) under both modes. A requested quantity was classed as materially in error when its relative error exceeded 2 percent, when an integer result was wrong, when a stated uncertainty quantity was in error by more than 50 percent, or when a finite answer was returned for an infeasible specification. Twenty-two problems were solved correctly in full in chat mode. Four contained a materially wrong quantity. This walkthrough recomputes the four failed quantities by execution and places each beside the recorded chat-mode answer.

data.text/markdown:
Step 2: Example 1: least-squares fit of 41 points

A batch reactor experiment for the reaction A ||(\rightarrow||) products records the concentration of A, ||(C_A||) in mol/L, at time ||(t||) in min, at 41 times from 0 to 200 min. The rate law is ||(-\mathrm{d}C_A/\mathrm{d}t = k C_A^{\,n}||), where ||(k||) is the rate constant, in ||((\mathrm{mol/L})^{1-n}\,\mathrm{min}^{-1}||), and ||(n||) is the reaction order, dimensionless. With initial concentration ||(C_{A0} = 1.80||) mol/L, the integrated rate law is ||[C_A(t) = \left( C_{A0}^{\,1-n} + (n-1)\,k\,t \right)^{1/(1-n)}||]Both parameters are determined by nonlinear least-squares fitting of all 41 points, minimising the sum of squared residuals between the measured and modelled concentrations. The fit is executed, not estimated: an iterative solver adjusts ||(k||) and ||(n||) until the sum of squared residuals is stationary.

data.text/markdown:
Step 3: Example 1: origin of the standard errors

The standard error of a fitted parameter measures the precision the data support for that parameter. For a least-squares fit with ||(N||) points and ||(p||) parameters, the covariance matrix of the parameters is ||(s^2 (\mathbf{J}^{\mathsf{T}} \mathbf{J})^{-1}||), where ||(\mathbf{J}||) is the Jacobian matrix of the model predictions with respect to the parameters, evaluated at all ||(N||) points, and ||(s^2||) is the residual variance, the residual sum of squares ||(\mathrm{SSE}||) divided by ||(N - p||). The standard error of each parameter is the square root of the corresponding diagonal entry. Every entry of ||(\mathbf{J}^{\mathsf{T}} \mathbf{J}||) is a sum over all 41 points, and the inverse mixes the two parameters, which are correlated (correlation coefficient 0.51 in this fit). No inspection of the residual scatter yields these numbers; the accumulation either is performed or is not. The chat-mode reply stated that the scatter of the residuals was propagated by judgement, and reported standard errors of 0.03 for ||(n||) and 0.002 for ||(k||).

data.text/markdown:
Step 4: Example 2: the root-mean-square error as an accumulation

The same experiment at pilot scale gives 25 points over 120 min. The root-mean-square error of a fit, ||(\mathrm{RMSE} = \sqrt{\mathrm{SSE}/N}||) in mol/L, is the quality figure of the fit itself. It is a sum of squared residuals over every point, divided by the number of points ||(N||) and square-rooted. The chat-mode reply reported fitted parameters of acceptable accuracy (||(n||) in error by 1.3 percent, ||(k||) by 1.9 percent) and a root-mean-square error of 0.013 mol/L. The value below is accumulated from the 25 residuals of the executed fit.

data.text/markdown:
Step 5: Example 3: annualised costs at full precision

Water at 20 °C (density ||(\rho = 998||) kg/m||(^3||), dynamic viscosity ||(\mu = 1.002 \times 10^{-3}||) Pa·s) is pumped at flow rate ||(Q = 0.110||) m||(^3||)/s through a horizontal line of length ||(L = 9000||) m. Two inside diameters are compared, ||(D = 0.28||) m and ||(D = 0.30||) m, both with absolute roughness ||(\varepsilon = 0.045||) mm. The Darcy friction factor ||(f||), dimensionless, follows the Colebrook equation in the Reynolds number ||(\mathrm{Re} = \rho v D / \mu||), where ||(v||) is the mean velocity in m/s; the pressure drop is ||(\Delta P = f (L/D)\, \rho v^2 / 2||) in Pa. Pumping power follows from ||(Q \Delta P||) divided by the combined efficiency 0.74; electricity costs 0.14 dollars per kWh over 8200 h per year. The installed cost is ||(2275\, D^{1.55}||) dollars per metre, annualised by the capital recovery factor 0.12 per year. The executed calculation carries full precision through every step.

data.text/markdown:
Step 6: Example 3: rounding before differencing

The saving is the difference of two totals of about 473,000 dollars/yr and is itself 0.034 percent of either total. A difference of near-equal quantities inherits the absolute error of its terms, not their relative error: rounding each total to the nearest ||(u||) dollars/yr admits an absolute error of up to ||(u||) in the difference, which is a relative error of up to ||(u / 161.08||) in the saving. The sweep below rounds the two executed totals at units from 0.01 to 1000 dollars/yr and differences the rounded values. At the chat-mode rounding unit of 100 dollars/yr, the difference of the rounded executed totals is 200 dollars/yr, an error of 24 percent; the chat-mode reply stated approximately 140 dollars/yr, which matches neither the exact saving nor the difference of its own stated totals (473,300 ||(-||) 473,200 ||(=||) 100 dollars/yr). The same amplification applies to the inputs. The last lines below change one input at a time by a modest amount and recompute the saving: it changes by thousands of dollars per year, and in three of the four cases ||(D = 0.30||) m becomes the cheaper diameter. The saving at the stated inputs is a test of arithmetic; for the design decision, the two diameters cost the same within the accuracy of the inputs.

data.text/markdown:
Step 7: Example 4: solution of the looped network

Water (properties as in Example 3) enters a looped pipe network at node A at 0.300 m||(^3||)/s. Demands (outflows) in m||(^3||)/s are: B 0.050, C 0.080, D 0.070, E 0.050, F 0.050. The pipes, with the flow direction taken as positive in each case, are A||(\rightarrow||)B (length 240 m, diameter 0.30 m), B||(\rightarrow||)C (180 m, 0.25 m), C||(\rightarrow||)D (220 m, 0.28 m), D||(\rightarrow||)A (260 m, 0.30 m), C||(\rightarrow||)E (150 m, 0.20 m), E||(\rightarrow||)F (170 m, 0.20 m), F||(\rightarrow||)D (190 m, 0.22 m), all with absolute roughness ||(\varepsilon = 0.045||) mm. The head loss in a pipe is ||(h = f (L/D)\, v^2 / (2g)||), with ||(g = 9.81||) m/s||(^2||) and ||(f||) from the Colebrook equation. Continuity at the nodes reduces the seven unknown flows to two loop corrections; the two loop equations (the signed head losses around each loop sum to zero) are solved by a Newton-type method. The loop residuals, printed below, are the verification. The same equations evaluated at the chat-mode flows leave about 0.08 m in the loop through CE, EF and FD, but the executed flows rounded to the same three decimals already leave about ||(-0.05||) m: at the quoted precision the residual check cannot separate the chat-mode error from rounding, and confirming the answer needs an independent solution of the network.

data.text/markdown:
Step 8: Example 4: the remainder at node E

Node E receives flow only from pipe CE and discharges its demand of 0.050 m||(^3||)/s and the flow in pipe EF. Continuity at node E therefore fixes the EF flow as a difference: ||(Q_{EF} = Q_{CE} - 0.050||) m||(^3||)/s. With ||(Q_{CE} = 0.04437||) m||(^3||)/s, the EF flow is ||(-0.00563||) m||(^3||)/s, the negative sign denoting flow from F toward E. The chat-mode Hardy–Cross iteration was accurate in absolute terms everywhere, and its node balance at E is exact (||(-0.005 = 0.045 - 0.050||)). Its error is in the CE flow, 0.045 against 0.04437 m||(^3||)/s (1.4 percent, within the 2 percent criterion); the same absolute error of 0.00063 m||(^3||)/s is 11 percent of the EF remainder. A quantity defined as the difference of two near-equal quantities inherits the absolute error of its parents, not their relative error — the same structure as the annual saving of Example 3, at the scale of a single node.

data.text/markdown:
Step 9: Anchor values and verification

The executed values are asserted against the independently verified record of the screening (each agent-mode result was verified by a second solver, an analytic identity, or a residual evaluation before the record was fixed). A failed assertion in this cell indicates drift between this walkthrough and the record. The four chat-mode failures share one structure: each failed quantity is an accumulation over all terms of a sum, a difference of near-equal quantities, or a remainder of near-cancelling quantities — and a stated uncertainty, which is an accumulation by definition. Quantities reached by iteration were accurate in chat mode throughout the screening; precision was lost at the points where exact accumulation or exact subtraction was the whole of the calculation. Chat mode gave a materially wrong number in 4 of the 26 problems, which is extremely bad for numerical results, and its replies did not say which numbers were wrong: chat mode should not be used for numerical work. The agent-mode values were also recomputed independently by agentic Claude Opus 5.5 with different methods (verify/ scripts; App panel, Independent verification), and all agree.
